One number for every kind of roof job

Roofing services in Houston fall into a few groups: fixing a problem, dealing with storm damage, putting on a new roof, and the specialty work on metal, flat and commercial roofs.

You do not have to know which group yours is in. Call, describe what you see, and the automated assistant passes your call to an independent, locally owned roofing contractor in greater Houston. That contractor inspects the roof and tells you whether it is a repair, a claim or a replacement, with its own written estimate.

The pages below are written to help you ask better questions, whoever you hire. None of them is a quote, and the line never prices or performs any work.

Repairs and leaks

Most calls start here: one weak spot on a roof that is otherwise sound. A careful repair finds the source, which is often uphill from the stain, and fixes the cause rather than smearing cement over it.

Not sure which service you need?

Start with what you can see from the ground and from inside. A roofer will work out the rest on the roof.

What you noticeStart with
A stain on the ceiling or a drip in the atticRoof leak repair
Water pouring in, or a tree or limb on the roofEmergency repair and tarping
Shingles in the yard after windWind damage
Dented gutters or vents after hailHail damage
A leak near a chimney, wall or skylightFlashing repair
A roof past 15 years, or buying or selling a houseRoof inspection
Curling shingles and granules in the guttersRoof replacement
Standing water on a flat roofFlat roof repair

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

What roofing services can I call about?

Repairs, leaks, flashing, emergency tarping, storm, hail and wind damage, inspections, full replacements, metal roofs, flat roofs and commercial roofs. Describe the problem when the assistant asks and your call goes to an independent roofing company that takes that kind of work in your area. Each service has its own page above.

Is a roofing contractor the same as this line?

No. A roofing contractor is the business that looks at the roof, prices the job and carries it out. Houston Expert Roofers only picks up the phone and hands your call to one. The contractor's contract, crew and workmanship warranty are between you and that company. The how it works page covers the details.

What roofing services are not offered through the line?

Calls are for roofs. Gutters on their own, solar panels, siding, remodeling, insurance advice, public adjusting and claim handling are not part of it. Texas licenses public adjusters through the Department of Insurance, and a roofer may not act as one on a property it works on. If you need help with a claim, read the roof insurance claims guide.

Do Houston roofing contractors do both homes and businesses?

Some do both and some specialize. Low-slope commercial roofs use different materials and permits from shingled homes. Say which you have when you call. The commercial roofing page explains the systems and the questions a property owner should ask.
